messages:
maria Gonzalez: paging — we're seeing a sharp tail-latency increase from the new rollout in eu-west1, +95th/99th up ~3x. Affected runtime pool: rwd-infer-v2.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — ID #INC-2354. Severity: P2. Trigger: latency spike on rwd-infer-v2 canary. Linked: monitoring/2354, traces/uv-2354.
ashley (oncall): grabbing it. what's the canary fraction and which flag was enabled?
sanjay Rao: canary fraction 5% traffic. Feature flag: fast-path-v2 was enabled for canary. Deployed earlier at 2354320770.
leo: logs show a surge of kernel fallback events (GPU -> CPU path) and batch sizes dropping to 1 for many requests. Sample log: ```ERROR kernel_select: incompatible_kernel -> fallback_to_generic at model.py:422```
maria Gonzalez: customer impact check: are there any 5xx increases or just latency?
sanjay Rao: 5xx stable. Most customers will see slow responses (timeouts for interactive apps if they had tight UI limits). No ingestion/backlog growth yet.
incident-bot: Page sent to oncall. Ashly (oncall) acknowledged at 2354321990.
ashley (oncall): oncall here — switching canary to 0% via rollout controller. Preparing rollback plan and quick flag flip. Any downstream caches to clear?
leo: don't clear caches yet — looks like prefix KV cache thrashing when kernel changes cause evictions. If we flip flag abruptly we might drop throughput further. Recommend step-down: route canary traffic to compatible model variant (v2-compat) first, then flip flag.
maria Gonzalez: agree. customer comms: drafting a status note: "Experiencing elevated latency after canary enabling fast-path-v2. Teams investigating; mitigation in progress."
sanjay Rao: commands: ```# scale down canary fraction to 0
kubectl patch rollout rwd-runtime --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/canary/weight","value":0}]'```
ashley (oncall): running that now. ```kubectl patch ...``` -> returned OK. Traffic should be shifting in ~10s. Monitoring...
ops-bot: ROUTE_UPDATE: canary weight -> 0. All new canary sessions draining.
leo: once traffic shifts, watch KV hit rate and batch size distribution. If we see batch size recover it's likely the new kernel selection was causing per-request path variability.
sanjay Rao: post-shift metrics: latency 95th dropped ~30% within 45s but 99th still elevated. Kernel fallback events decreased but some persistent ones remain tied to long seq length requests.
maria Gonzalez: we should enable the emergency feature-flag rollback for fast-path-v2 as well to prevent future rollouts from re-enabling it. Who can flip?
ashley (oncall): I can flip. Where's the flag service?
sanjay Rao: flag key `features.fast_path_v2` in config-service. REST call: ```POST /flags/fast_path_v2/rollout {"state":"off","actor":"oncall"}``` Auth: service token.
ashley (oncall): did the POST -> 200. Confirmed flag off across regions.
incident-bot: FLAG_EVENT: features.fast_path_v2 -> off by ashley (oncall) at 2354322009.
leo: good. batch sizes rebounded to expected distribution after flag flip and route shift. Throughput returning to baseline but a small backlog spike as drains complete.
maria Gonzalez: preparing incident summary for customers: impact window ~2354320770 - 2354321990, increased tail latency for small % of requests, no 5xx. Mitigation: immediate canary traffic removal and feature flag disable.
sanjay Rao: root cause hypothesis: kernel selection heuristics in the fast-path-v2 variant mis-classified certain long-sequence requests resulting in fallback and inefficient KV cache usage -> batch fragmentation. Next steps: reproduce with synthetic traces, add additional guards in kernel selector, and add a preflight that checks batch distribution before enabling fast-path on rollout.
ashley (oncall): handing off to runtime team for postmortem and follow-up. @leo @sanjay take lead. I'll keep incident open for now and will update when official postmortem is posted.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity downgraded to P3 at 2354322013.
maria Gonzalez: noted. final note: no major customer-visible failures, a few users with strict latency SLOs may have seen timeouts; outreach queued. Closing in ~1h unless new regressions. :white_check_mark:
